neurotransmitters, neurotrophics, and Ca2+ channels may interact at the level of synaptic contacts in order to modulate the formation, maturation, and stabilization of synaptic contacts.
neurotrophins may participate in the development of synaptic contacts and in the maturation of synapses in the adult, but this participation is likely to be complex and multifaceted.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neurotrophin/neurotransmitter interaction is a fundamental mechanism in the development and plasticity of the nervous system.
neurotrophin activity may be a key element in the establishment of synaptic connectivity, maturation of synaptic function and refinement of synapse efficacy.
neurotrophins are not only survival factors but also play an active role during development in the formation of functional neuronal connections and the maturation of the synapse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neurotrophins are not only important for the survival and differentiation of neuronal cells, but also for their synaptic connectivity.
